A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Lean-STaR. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original miniF2F experiments with trained Lean-CoT and Lean-STaR models, including ablations, budget analyses and generated proofs.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds LeanDojo evaluation, decoding comparisons, an expanded ablation and proof-overlap analysis.

M1.justification: The proposed retrospective rationale generation, thought-augmented fine-tuning, successful-proof filtering, expert iteration and trajectory-sampling inference remain unchanged. Joint versus continued training was already examined in v1.

E1.justification: v1 uses LeanDojo/Mathlib for training and miniF2F for evaluation. v4 additionally evaluates a random 320-example subset of LeanDojo4-v9-test with novel premises (Table 1), substantially broadening evaluation beyond Olympiad-style miniF2F problems.

E2.justification: The named benchmark baselines are retained. v4 Table 8 adds best-first search with sampled token decoding and explicitly compares search variants against trajectory sampling for thought-augmented models. Table 3 also extends the expert-iteration-without-CoT comparator to InternLM2-base; v1's corresponding ablation covered InternLM2-plus only.

E3.justification: Existing training budgets and principal pass@K settings remain. Added protocols specify the 320-example test subset, controlled search/decoding comparisons (Table 8), and exact/first-tactic proof matching (Table 5). Section 3.3 also changes the stated search priority from maximum cumulative log probability to maximum cumulative negative log probability; this documents a changed rule without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds a proof-overlap audit addressing possible leakage and a controlled search-versus-sampling analysis, while extending the no-CoT expert-iteration ablation to the base model. Category, budget and joint-training analyses are retained, including those moved to appendices. The generated aime_1983_p2 proof example is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed-based variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both retain the description of constructing K=64 from two 32-attempt batches. The added proof counts are descriptive results, not a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial results, including LeanDojo rates of 29.7% for InternLM2-7b and 39.4% for Lean-STaR iteration 2, a 30.7% base-model no-CoT expert-iteration result, search-comparison scores and proof-overlap counts. Existing headline miniF2F table values remain unchanged. The stronger-model discussion corrects 39.8% in v1 Section 4.5 to 40.9% in v4 Section 4.3, matching both versions' tables.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the mathematical search-priority definition from maximizing sum log p to maximizing sum negative log p, reversing the ordering under the stated definitions. The MDP formulation, thought marginalization and expected-reward objective remain unchanged; no new theoretical guarantees are introduced.

C1.justification: v4 removes state-of-the-art claims from the abstract, introduction and conclusion, retaining claims of improvement over base models. The central contributions—interleaving thoughts and tactics, the thought-augmented dataset and expert iteration—remain the same.

C2.justification: New Appendix C discusses possible GPT-4/InternLM exposure to miniF2F and argues that leakage is unlikely based on benchmark practice and proof dissimilarity. Existing interpretations concerning thought diversity, training variants and computational limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v4 omits v1's explicit 10-minute sampling limit, 20-minute stronger-model search limit and 60,000-example training count for the no-CoT expert-iteration baseline. These are losses of reproducibility information, not evidence that execution changed. The generation prompt, hardware disclosure and main training details remain available.

R1.justification: Positioning narrows from state-of-the-art superiority to improvement over base models, and the leakage audit explicitly follows Thakur et al. The related-work survey otherwise remains stable. The added Thakur 2024 reference identifies the same arXiv work as the existing 2023 entry, rather than a distinct new work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. Two experimental-analysis subsections move to the appendices, with corresponding renumbering and cross-reference updates. Citation style, author order and affiliation text change. The relocated category analysis has a malformed 'sectionPerformance Analysis' heading in v4.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a different conference layout and substantially reorganizes displays. Table 1 gains a benchmark column, v1 Table 5 becomes a two-model comparison, and new leakage and decoding tables appear. The rationale example and category/budget tables move to appendices. Existing figure artwork is retained.

improvement.justification: The additional LeanDojo evaluation, base-model control and explicit decoding comparison strengthen empirical support for the unchanged approach (v4 Tables 1, 3 and 8), while removing the state-of-the-art claim improves calibration. The gain is limited by omitted time limits and the reversed search-priority formula. Appendix C raises a relevant validity concern, but proof dissimilarity does not establish absence of pretraining exposure.
